rows: Ladies and gentlemen, look at the man who keeps asking for a spotlight. Then look at me.
Brawling? Watch me do it in front of the biggest crowd in the building.
A bold entrance runs on nerve, and I have plenty. I have plenty of it, and I am happy to share.
Slow it down if you must. The people came to see a star, and I am the star.
The people are the show. Give them a performance they will talk about on the bus home.
Here is the crux: this is my moment, and I am taking it.
I am the centre of the show's biggest moment, and nobody here needs me to say otherwise.
Gaze upon this pose, ladies and gentlemen. It was made for photographs, and you are going to be in every one.
A technique, you say, with the crowd watching. Your technique is missing from the programme, so show it to the people.
Strikes? I invented the noise. You invented the silence.
Risky? Yes. Worth it? Only if the crowd gets its money's worth.
Stalling is not a show. Give them a show.
The people paid to see a contest. Make it one they will want to see again.
You want to be the main attraction. Stand next to me and see how it looks.
You are proud of your {strength}, and the crowd can see it. It is a fine act, and I will be watching it closely.
I have seen your {strength} and I have a better angle on it.
You kept your head, I grant you. Lovely. It makes the bravado look better when I bring it.
Calm is a costume too. I will take it off for the crowd.
I could shout, and the crowd would shout back. I would rather save my voice for the finish.
One fall, and the whole place will rise. Keep me down and I will bow to you in front of everyone.
On the mat I will be the one getting the applause for every move.
Grounded or standing, the spotlight stays on me.
Stay in front of me if you want the attention. It is a hard job.
A reasonable answer, for once. Now the crowd wants more.
The microphone is still waiting for you. The people noticed, and so did I.
Very well, I grant you that much. Let us give the crowd something to cheer.
I will grant you that, with a bow. The bell is calling.
I will give everything I have until the bell. After that the crowd decides.
I am here to put on a show, and I intend to do it properly.
Whatever happens, the people will remember where I stood.
Nothing is decided yet, and that is what makes it exciting.
I have one more thing for the crowd. Watch when the bell goes.
I can give them a splendid performance, but I cannot produce an incident that proves the charge. That part of the act comes out.
A flourish is not an explanation. You've asked for particulars, and I haven't any that stand up.
Very well. Remove that from the bill. We still have a performance to give.
Good. No need for a villain in that particular story. The audience came to see us wrestle.
The paying public will see who can turn the spotlight into a winning performance. That is the only billing I need.
Watch the main attraction when the bell goes. A good pose is one thing; holding the other wrestler down is another.
Ladies and gentlemen, you have heard the accusation. What can we actually demonstrate before this audience?
Forget the gossip column. What can we put on tonight's show that the people can judge for themselves?
Ladies and gentlemen, you've heard the plan for stopping my {strength}. Now watch what happens when I actually use them.
You have studied my {strength} from your seat in the stalls. Try dealing with them when you're sharing the spotlight.
Very well! Even a master of ceremonies cannot announce a result before it exists.
I grant the correction. Let the audience witness the spectacle rather than take my account on faith.
Ladies and gentlemen, give those years a round of applause. Now watch what happens when the spotlight moves.
You've got a career worth introducing. That doesn't mean you get to write my introduction for me.
Experience teaches you when the crowd is ready for the next big moment.
I've learned how to keep the attention when a match goes off the script.
Ladies and gentlemen, my opponent has been watching my performances. Now let's see whether they can handle the live show.
You've studied the highlights. The star of this show has rather more material than that.
I study the whole performance, including the bit where my opponent thinks the spotlight has moved.
Preparation means having something ready when the audience expects one thing and the match gives us another.
